rationale: The Latin anchors *corruerunt* (collapsed/fell down) and *cum fragore dissilire* (burst apart with a crash) point to a sudden, catastrophic structural failure — walls and things ceasing to hold together. Among the candidates, fail.v.04 ("stop operating or functioning") best captures this sense of something giving way and ceasing to function/stand, as opposed to human-agentive or financial failure senses. The physical, concrete nature of bursting/collapsing aligns most closely with a system or structure failing (stopping functioning) rather than any of the more abstract or personal senses.
